column6: The original equates faith with persuasion, while the back-translation equates faith with trustful obedience, which shifts the focus from a cognitive belief to an action-oriented understanding of faith.
column7: Faith is a bedrock concept in Christianity. Faith is such a commonly used word in Christianity that sometimes the meaning of the word is supplanted by subtle misconceptions and wrong understanding. But it’s not something you can hold in your hands-it’s something formed in your heart as you come to trust God. Persuasion is belief.
column8: Faith is a cornerstone concept of the Christian faith. The word “faith” is used so frequently in Christianity that at times its meaning is replaced by subtle misunderstandings and misconceptions. But it is not something you can hold in your hand—it is something formed within you as you learn to trust God. Trustful obedience is faith.

column7: Faith misrepresented abstractly has no specific conviction or persuasion. This is often evident with a bit of probing as this representation of faith cannot be made specific. If you ask, ‘what do you believe’ or ‘why do you believe’ the person with this understanding of faith often cannot clarify beyond ‘I believe’. 1 Peter 3:15 says we should be ready to give an answer for the hope that is in us.
column8: When faith is misrepresented in an abstract way, it lacks concrete beliefs or obedient trust. A little probing reveals this, because such a portrayal of faith cannot be made specific. If you ask, “What do you believe?” or “Why do you believe?”, people who think this way often can say little beyond “I believe.” 1 Peter 3:15 says we should always be ready to give a defense for the hope that is in us.

column6: Both paragraphs convey the same doctrinal message that obedience is prioritized over sacrifice, emphasizing God's grace when one strays from the right path. The back-translation maintains the original intent and logical relationships without altering the meaning.
column7: A truth consistent since the Old Testament is that obedience is better than sacrifice. It's better to correctly follow what we should do, than to need to make a sacrifice to make up for what we did not do correctly. Thankfully there is grace from God when we stray from the path, miss the mark (sin), and need to turn back towards God.
